summary.text: Brett Guthrie is the Republican incumbent for Kentucky's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2008. A West Point graduate and former Army officer, he worked in his family's Bowling Green manufacturing business and served in the Kentucky State Senate before entering Congress. He chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce in the 119th Congress.

paragraphs.text: Guthrie was born in 1964 in Florence, Alabama, according to Ballotpedia. His official biography describes his family's manufacturing business in Bowling Green, Kentucky.
He earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987 and a master's degree in Public and Private Management from Yale University in 1997.

He served in the U.S. Army from 1987 to 1990 and in the Army Reserve from 1990 to 2002; his official biography says he was a Field Artillery Officer in the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault) at Fort Campbell.
After his Army service, Guthrie joined Trace Die Cast, a Bowling Green manufacturing business started by his father, according to his official biography.
First elected to public office in 1998, he represented the 32nd District in the Kentucky State Senate from 1999 until his election to Congress in 2008.
He has served Kentucky's 2nd District in the U.S. House since 2009.
In the 119th Congress, Guthrie chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, a panel with jurisdiction over energy, the environment, health care, telecommunications and consumer product safety.

According to his official biography, he has served as a Deputy Whip within the House Republican Conference for three terms, and he is married to the former Beth Clemmons, with whom he has three children and several grandchildren.
